name: Embout d'échappement ovale, variante titane F1
description: Same double-wall geometry as the IN625 F0 variant, screened in titanium. Selected by the repository titanium screening as the only part in the catalogue where both titanium and additive manufacturing win without running into the safety class. The alloy is deliberately not fixed in the identifier: Ti-6Al-4V and Ti-6242 are both screened, and a temperature that has never been measured separates them.

classification.intended_use: CAD, DfAM, flow, thermal, pressure and modal screening; no manufacturing for fitting and no vehicle installation authorized

provenance.record_license: All rights reserved (see LICENSE) for the concept, the script and the calculations; no photograph, trademark, PET illustration or commercial geometry redistributed

sources.title: FVD - 993 narrow-body oval stainless tips
sources.notes: FVD declares 120 mm at the widest, 85 mm at the tallest, stainless construction and C2/C4/RS applications. No inlet diameter, length, angle, thickness or datum. See SRC-FVD-993-EXHAUST-TIPS-DIMENSIONS.

sources.title: PorscheFanatics - register of declared materials
sources.notes: Documents 993 Turbo exhaust offerings declared in IN625; material precedent only, with no geometry and no fitment transfer. See SRC-PORSCHEFANATICS-993-IN625-EXHAUST-REGISTER.

sources.title: EOS NickelAlloy IN625 material data sheet
sources.notes: M 290 40 µm screening values, dependent on orientation and post-processing. See SRC-EOS-IN625-MATERIAL-DATA.

sources.title: Special Metals - INCONEL alloy 625
sources.notes: Reference wrought thermal properties, never an LPBF allowables card. See SRC-SPECIAL-METALS-INCONEL-625.

material.grade: Ti-6Al-4V if the actual temperature allows it; Ti-6242 otherwise, but with no supplier identified
material.standard: ASTM F2924 for PBF-LB Ti-6Al-4V; AMS 4975/4976 for wrought Ti-6242

post_processing: trimming, support removal and rework of the attachments
stress relief heat treatment, 800 °C 2 h under argon on the EOS Ti64 route
controlled depowdering of the 2.7 mm annular channel, borescope inspection required
external surface finish to be defined, the tip is visible
supplier_requirements: Material certificate, powder lot and number of reuses
Proposed orientation and support topology, with justification
Evidence of depowdering of the annular channel, by borescope or tomography
Documented heat treatment and delivery condition
Layer thickness used and coupon properties at that thickness

titanium.alloy: Ti-6Al-4V primary candidate, Ti-6242 high-temperature fallback
titanium.heat_treatment: 800 °C 2 h under argon for the EOS Ti64 route; not fixed for Ti-6242
inspection: dimensional inspection of the outlet envelope
borescope inspection of the annular channel
titanium.galvanic_isolation: Titanium/stainless steel couple at the outlet mounting: to be addressed; titanium is noble and stainless follows it closely, but moisture and road salt remain present.

known_limits: The 427 °C temperature that decides the alloy is a synthetic input of the F0 screening, never measured on a vehicle.
Only the 120 x 85 mm outlet envelope is published; length, inlet interface and slip-fit depth are assumptions.
Depowdering of the 2.7 mm annular channel is checked only by the 1 mm voxel screening, a resolution too coarse to conclude.
No reviewed orientation, no supplier supports, no machine file.
No strength, thermal cycling, acoustic or vehicle fitting test.
